# Benchmarks

```{r model_family_header, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
acousticTS:::.model_family_header(
  family = "dwba",
  pages = c(
    Overview = "index.html",
    Theory = "dwba-theory.html",
    Implementation = "dwba-implementation.html",
    Benchmarks = "dwba-benchmarks.html",
    Validation = "dwba-validation.html"
  )
)
```

DWBA benchmark comparisons use the canonical weakly scattering targets from Jech et al. [@Jech_2015]. These are benchmark anchors for the approximation, not exact guarantees for arbitrary segmented bodies.

| Geometry | Max abs. $\Delta$ vs benchmark (dB) | Mean abs. $\Delta$ vs benchmark (dB) | Elapsed (s) |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|
| Weakly scattering sphere | 16.17744 | 0.29031 | 0.74 |
| Weakly scattering prolate spheroid | 0.04993 | 0.01735 | 5.11 |
| Weakly scattering cylinder | 2.28194 | 0.06664 | 2.53 |

The largest absolute dB differences are concentrated near deep nulls. For physical-strength comparisons, `sigma_bs` residuals should be checked alongside `TS`.

## Software implementation comparison

The segmented krill benchmark is also compared to the `echoSMs` implementation on the published sweep. This is a software benchmark, not a validation-method result.

| Benchmark comparison | Target | Frequency range | Mean abs. $\Delta TS$ (dB) | Max abs. $\Delta TS$ (dB) |
|:--|:--|:--|--:|--:|
| acousticTS vs `echoSMs` | Segmented krill | Published sweep | 0.42284 | 1.01167 |
| McGehee et al. (1998) vs `echoSMs` | Segmented krill | Published sweep | 0.42284 | 1.01167 |

## Published segmented-body benchmark

The same segmented krill target is also checked against the published McGehee et al. calculation [@mcgehee_software]. The case matches the segment positions, local radii, weak-scattering contrasts, orientation, and frequency grid.

| Benchmark comparison | Target | Frequency range | Mean abs. $\Delta TS$ (dB) | Max abs. $\Delta TS$ (dB) |
|:--|:--|:--|--:|--:|
| acousticTS vs McGehee et al. (1998) | Segmented krill | Published sweep | 1.23e-05 | 4.33e-05 |
